summary: Short-lived CI tokens evicted leading to intermittent runner job failures during KMS key rolling update
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled KMS key rolling update on 2026-03-08, a subset of short-lived CI tokens used by self-hosted runners were rejected shortly after issuance. This caused intermittent job failures across multiple release pipelines (no global outage but high error rate for ~40 minutes).

Impact:
- ~18% of scheduled CI jobs in prod-us-east failed with 401/403 during the window.
- Several long-running release jobs were retried and timed out, delaying two releases by ~2 hours.
- No secrets were exposed; failures were authentication rejections.

Timeline (key events):
- 2026-03-08 02:05 UTC: KMS rotation started in us-east.
- 2026-03-08 02:12 UTC: First CI job failures observed (401 from auth-service).
- 2026-03-08 02:20 UTC: Pager alert to #support and on-call SRE.
- 2026-03-08 02:30 UTC: Investigation identified token verification failures against rotated key.
- 2026-03-08 02:54 UTC: Quick mitigation applied (auth-service hotfix to accept previous signing key for 15m).
- 2026-03-08 03:00 UTC: Runner restart/workaround rolled out and job success rate returned to baseline.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-east-1
- Affected CI runner pool: r2-large (self-hosted fleet)
- Auth stack: auth-service v1.14.2, token provider service v0.9.7
- KMS: AWS-KMS key alias: alias/redwood-ci-keys (rotation schedule)

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Issue an OIDC short-lived token from token-provider immediately after KMS key rotation event.
2. Attempt job registration/heartbeat from a runner using the new token.
3. Observe token verification rejection in auth-service logs referencing missing signature key id.

Observed behavior:
- auth-service logs: "token verification failed: unknown key id: k-20260308-1"
- client (runner) logs: repeated registration attempts, then transient 401s, then eventual reconnect after token refresh or restart.

Expected behavior:
- Tokens issued shortly before or during KMS rotation should validate against either the active key or the previous key for a short grace window, avoiding mass evictions.

Relevant logs and dashboards:
- grafana: ci-runner/error-rate (spike 02:12-02:55 UTC)
- kibana: auth-service logs filter: "token verification failed"
- slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234567/p1678387200000)
comments: Maya Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-08 02:25 UTC: Noticed increase in 401s hitting multiple release pipelines. Creating incident. Attaching first log snippets.
Ethan Cole (Assignee/SRE) - 2026-03-08 02:33 UTC: Correlated with KMS rotation event from infra calendar. Pulling auth-service logs now.
Lena Ortiz (SRE) - 2026-03-08 02:38 UTC: auth-service shows rejection due to unknown key id. Token provider appears to issue tokens referencing the new key id immediately after rotation.

Arjun Mehta (Auth Eng) - 2026-03-08 02:45 UTC: Confirmed token signature verification only uses current key set; previous key shadowing not applied. Preparing emergency patch to accept previous key for short window.
Priya Singh (Release Eng) - 2026-03-08 02:56 UTC: Restarted a sample set of runners in r2-large pool; jobs resumed successfully. Will coordinate larger restart after hotfix is deployed.
Ethan Cole - 2026-03-08 03:05 UTC: Hotfix deployed to auth-service (PR #4823). Monitoring for recurrence. Filing postmortem and runbook updates.
Maya Patel - 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Added proposed postmortem notes and next steps. Assigned follow-ups to release engineering and infra.
Arjun Mehta - 2026-03-11 14:20 UTC: Follow-up PR to token-provider to pre-warm key cache and delay new-token issuance by 60s during rotation: PR #4990
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: token-provider begins issuing tokens signed with the new KMS key immediately after rotation; auth-service does not accept previous key signatures because keyset cache was not updated/retained.

Key evidence: auth-service rejects list includes key id k-20260308-1; token-provider logs show tokens referencing k-20260308-1 issued at 02:11 UTC while auth-service keyset still referenced k-20260307-2.
Reproducer confirmed on staging by simulating KMS rotation and querying token issuance + verification sequence.
Scope: affects self-hosted runner pools that rely on short-lived tokens (TTL 10m). Hosted API tokens unaffected.
Risk analysis: high for in-flight CI pipelines during rotation windows; low risk to security (no key material exfiltration detected).
resolution: Applied hotfix to auth-service to accept tokens signed by previous key for a configurable grace window (default 15 minutes). Deployed 2026-03-08 02:54 UTC.
Restarted r2-large runner fleet in phases to allow token re-registration; this drained the backlog without causing new rollout collisions.

Updated KMS rotation runbook: require 'ci-token-safe' precheck and pre-warm token-provider key cache before initiating rotation. Document added: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/12345/KMS+rotation+runbook

Implemented follow-ups: token-provider change to delay issuance of tokens signed by the new key for 60s and to pre-fetch previous key material; added monitoring alert on token verification error rate > 1% in 5m.

Post-incident tasks: (1) change default short-lived token TTL from 10m -> 15m to reduce churn during rotations; (2) add runbook step to coordinate runner restarts when rotation is unavoidable; (3) schedule an internal dry-run of KMS rotation next month.
Status: all immediate mitigation applied and validated. Postmortem to be published; follow-ups assigned to infra and release-eng for Q2 sprint.
